description: This report, led by Elisabeth Krausmann of the European Commission Joint Research Centre (JRC) and published in 2015 (DOI 10.2788/211456), presents the findings of the Space weather and rail workshop held in London on 16 and 17 September 2015, organised by the JRC, the Swedish Civil Contingencies Agency, the UK Department for Transport and the US National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration. Coverage: while most space weather research focuses on the power grid, satellite navigation and aviation, railway networks are also a concern: anomalies in signalling systems have been observed during geomagnetic storms, and rail depends on power, communications and increasingly on GNSS for timing and positioning. Participants came from the railway sector, insurance, European and North American government agencies, academia and the European Commission. Format and access: a report PDF linked from the JRC repository. Licence and cost: free; marked as a public document that can be shared. Caveats: workshop findings, not measured impacts; the abstract was the part read. The identified dependencies can define space weather hazard exposure and resilience scenarios for rail signalling and traction. It relates to the UK railway signalling misoperation study and the Lloyd's-Cambridge extreme space weather scenario in the catalogue.
